scores.evidence: 'Morning' section opens with 'If you only caught the last four laps on Sunday, you saw the pass' — narration before verdict
'Until next week' is a classic wrap-up paragraph restating standings and teasing next race
'Morning' section adds 'Here's what the data does say' — a bridging sentence doing work headings should handle
Lap-28 section clusters: 13.7s behind, ~31s green-flag cost, 18s cheaper, 40-odd laps old — numbers pile up rather than deploy singly
'I don't think so... it might not have... on that simple extrapolation' — explicit, graded, owned
Russell is the sustained benchmark throughout; every Antonelli datum is measured against his team-mate
Track-limits deletion message quoted verbatim mid-analysis, complicating the closing narrative precisely
'He'd already got seven of those back in two laps when the red flag came out' — mild sequence narration assumes reader needs the recap
'Closing wasn't passing, not at Monza' and 'Russell kept the lead and Antonelli finishes second in the quicker car' — flat, dry, effective
'Here's what the data does say' — sentence about the piece itself; first person elsewhere is appropriately restrained
No introductions, no definitions; VSC, track limits, tyre compounds all handled without gloss
Paragraphs consistently 2-4 sentences; 'The pace was real. The cheap stop is what let him spend it.' exemplary
'At green-flag speed the same stop would have cost about 31 seconds, going by the race's median pit-lane time. That's 18 seconds cheaper' — long/short alternation visible
Winners/losers section gives Antonelli two sentences and Verstappen two — the race winner should command more density than third place

top_fixes: Kill 'Until next week' entirely — standings and Madrid tease are the exact summary paragraph the rules prohibit; the piece ends when Pérez's stewards note ends

Open 'Morning' on the verdict ('The red flag restarted the race from a position Antonelli could exploit; everything before lap 3 is prologue') and delete the narration-first sentences and the meta-line 'Here's what the data does say'

In the VSC section, choose one number to carry the argument — the 18-second delta — and let the others arrive only if they're doing distinct work; currently 13.7s, ~31s, 18s, and '40-odd laps' crowd the same paragraph and read like a spreadsheet
